text: Okay, now that said, there are actually many different types of modulations. Over the years, researchers have been able to design modulations that are more and more complex and efficient in carrying bits. An example is this one, where the signals in the constellation vary not just by one parameter, but by two parameters. For example, in this case, they vary by phase and amplitude. So each signal, as you can see, corresponds to a certain phase and a certain amplitude. Okay, so they are called QAM modulations, and they create these constellations where signals differ depending on the symbols that we transmit by both amplitude and phase. For example, in this kind of modulation constellation, we have sixteen signals. So it means that each signal can carry four bits. Okay, so we can increase further the number of bits. Consider nowadays in advanced wireless communications, we are using also 256 QAM constellations. Okay, so eight bits can be carried by one signal. So we are increasing more and more the number of bits that can be.
